haiku-low.q1: Replica row_count decides: 10,000 or fewer returns a 200 CSV download built in-request; more returns 202, and a background job emails a download link.
haiku-low.q2: It returns the existing active export with its original filters, not a new one. Exports idle 6+ hours are failed and replaced.
haiku-low.q3: Up to 24 hours, capped at the file's remaining life. The bucket's lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after creation.
haiku-low.q4: Three attempts, retried after 60 and 300 seconds. Then the export is marked failed, parts are aborted, and an export_failed email is sent.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica. Report rows and reports.row_count are read only from it, never from the primary.
haiku-low.q6: Stored in export_jobs on the primary. The page polls /exports/latest every 5 seconds while queued or running, and reads it on every load.
haiku-low.q7: Streams 5,000-row replica pages into 16 MB multipart parts, checkpointing each. Holds only one page and one buffer; never writes to local disk.
haiku-low.q8: Committed parts are kept. The next attempt resumes after the saved checkpoint (next_row_id), and an uncommitted part is re-uploaded under the same part number.
haiku-low.q9: Saved on the export_jobs row as normalised filters and cols strings. The job reads them from that row; its payload carries only export_id.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running on export_jobs. The second insert conflicts and returns the active export.
haiku-low.q11: Status must be done, with the object complete and storage_key set. On rerun, it emails if email_sent_at is empty; otherwise it returns without action.
haiku-low.q12: Nothing is stored, and the body is sent only when complete, so the error returns no body. The user clicks again.

sonnet.q1: By reports.row_count read from the read replica: 10,000 or fewer goes to the small path, above goes to the large path. Small path: 200 with the CSV as the response body (text/csv attachment, built in the request, sent only when complete). Large path: 202 Accepted with {export_id, status, filters}, and a background job writes the file; the user gets an email with a download link (and the page polls and offers the link). Also, a small-path request that reads a 10,001st filtered row drops its buffer and gets the same 202 large-path response.
sonnet.q2: The insert of a new export_jobs row hits the partial unique index (one active export per user and report). On conflict, no new export starts; the existing active export is returned with 202 {export_id, status, filters}, and the page says which view (filters) it covers, which may be the older filters. Exception: if the active row has had no updates for over 6 hours (stale guard), it is aborted and marked failed ('stalled') and a new one is inserted.
sonnet.q3: The emailed link is a signed URL with ttl = min(86400, object_created_at + 7 days - now), so up to 24 hours and never longer than the object lives. The bucket's lifecycle rule deletes each object 7 days after it is created. Multipart uploads not completed within 24 hours are discarded. The export_jobs and export_parts rows are not cleaned up.
sonnet.q4: 3 attempts total (retries after 60 s, then 300 s). After the 3rd fails, on_final_failure runs: unless status is already done, the status is set to failed with a short error, the multipart upload is aborted, and an 'export_failed' email is sent (if that send fails it is logged). The page shows failed. If the handler itself fails, the row stays running until the 6-hour stale guard clears it.
sonnet.q5: The read replica, for all report rows and counts, never the primary (no fallback; 503 if replica unreachable). Only export state (export_jobs/export_parts) is read from the primary.
sonnet.q6: In the export_jobs table (and export_parts) on the primary database. The page polls every 5 seconds while the export is queued or running, via GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest, which returns the caller's most recent export (status, filters, created_at, attempt, error, fresh download_url if done and unexpired). On a later page load it calls the same endpoint, minting a new signed URL each time, or shows 'This export has expired. Export again.' if the object is past 7 days.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads the replica in keyset pages of 5,000 rows (row_id > checkpoint), builds CSV in a byte buffer, cuts a 16 MB part when the buffer reaches 16 MB after a complete row, uploads it as a multipart-upload part, and commits it. Only one page and one 16 MB buffer are in memory, and nothing is written to local disk. About 57 parts at ~450 bytes per row, under the 10,000-part limit. After 20 minutes an attempt stops starting new parts and enqueues a new job that resumes from the checkpoint. Finally complete_multipart assembles the object.
sonnet.q8: Parts already committed (saved in export_parts, with next_row_id as checkpoint) are kept. An uncommitted part is regenerated and re-uploaded with the same part number, replacing it. A buffer not yet uploaded is lost and regenerated. The next attempt (same payload, rerun of handler) reloads the row and resumes from next_row_id (the last row_id in the last committed part), or from the start if null. It restarts from scratch (old upload aborted, parts deleted) only if there is no upload or the upload is over 20 hours old.
sonnet.q9: They are normalised with the same parser/validator as the rows API and stored as the filters and cols columns of the export_jobs row on the primary, inserted at click time. The job payload is only {export_id}; the job reads filters and cols from the row, so they cannot disagree.
sonnet.q10: A partial unique index on export_jobs (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running, enforced by the database on the single-statement insert. The loser's insert conflicts and it returns the active export.
sonnet.q11: The upload must have been completed (complete_multipart) and the row conditionally set to status = done with storage_key and object_created_at; done is written only after the object is complete. On a rerun, the job loads the row: if status = done and email_sent_at is empty, it goes straight to Step 10 and sends the email (no re-export); if done and email_sent_at is set, it returns without doing anything (duplicate delivery). The email_sent_at is set after the send succeeds.
sonnet.q12: Nothing is stored and no job exists. If a database error or the 60-second API limit hits before the body is complete, the request returns an error with no body (the body is only sent when complete, so no truncated file is saved). The user clicks again.
